evidenceSummary.excerpt: During the childhood of Apollo and Diana the goddess Latona lived happily on the island of Delos, and forgot all her early misfortunes in the joy of her children.
Latona was proud of her children's fame, and boasted of it far and wide.

When Latona received the message she was so enraged at the insult that her desire for revenge knew no bounds. She called Apollo and Diana to her side and commanded them to go forth and slay the children of Niobe.
Over her fallen body the wretched Niobe wept so long that the gods at last felt pity for her grief, and changed her into stone.
Though the goddess Diana[14] spent most of her daylight hours in hunting, it was not often that she exercised her skill to such cruel purpose as was shown in the case of poor Niobe.
